title: Fourier coefficient of a coordinate slice
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f:\\{-1,1\\}^{n+1}\\to\\mathbb R$, let $b\\in\\{-1,1\\}$, and let $S\\subseteq\\{1,\\ldots,n\\}$. Write $S^+\\subseteq\\{1,\\ldots,n+1\\}$ for the set obtained by shifting every coordinate in $S$ up by one. The Fourier coefficient of the slice of $f$ with first coordinate fixed to $b$, at $S$, equals the Fourier coefficient of $f$ at $S^+$ plus $b$ times its coefficient at $S^+\\cup\\{1\\}$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a real-valued function on the $(n+1)$-dimensional sign cube
$S$ is a subset of the $n$ coordinates
